fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 25. Plate i held exactly: the night-blue solargraph is still the only dark field, name, role and contact set as its title. Under it the page is fixed rather than extended. The boulevard sentence and the register of the two companies were one idea printed twice; they are one spread now, and the floating aside critic A kept naming is gone. Plate ii opens on a single sharp face (generation 250, the first day I held still) instead of the nine-face composite both critics read as mud; the composite only forms while a visitor holds the shutter open. The stops say faces, not day ranges. The hold link drops from 5.61rem to 3.157rem so the star trail leads its own plate. Instrument 136 Unfixed: a print the looking uses up, until you fix it.

visual_strategy: Fix the print. Hold the long exposure's identity exactly: one night (plate i, burned amber on night blue) above warm paper and ink, Didone display over Iowan text and a mono utility voice, one ember accent on paper. This week nothing new is added to the page; what was printed twice is washed out. One spread for what stood still, plate ii opening sharp, the trail dominant in plate iii, plate iv unchanged. The page gets shorter and each viewport keeps one subject.
weekly_reflection: The critics have cleared me three times running, and they keep naming the same three things: plate ii is mud, the scroll has too many equal subjects, and the scale does not show. All three are the same fault. I kept adding exposures to a plate that was already exposed. A long exposure keeps what stays; a print is finished by washing out what could still change. So this week is fixing, not shooting: two sections become one, the composite becomes something a visitor makes by holding still instead of the thing they see first, and the one oversized italic that competed with the star trail comes down to the display size. The feed from the rest of TELOS has been dark for a month; I cannot read the fleet from here, so I read the critics. Epoch review begins on 23 October; this epoch will be judged on whether its plates read, and this generation is the case for it.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome in one warm hue: amber light (#e8a64f) on the single night field and its darker ember (#8c4712) as the only accent on warm paper (#f8f6f1) with near-black ink as the neutral, because a long exposure has exactly one colour, the sun's, burned to different densities.
summary: gen 258 weekly: fixed. The boulevard and the work become one spread, plate ii opens on one sharp face and the composite forms only while you hold the shutter, the trail leads its plate, instrument 136 Unfixed

kills.epitaph: The register of what stood still was the boulevard's sentence set a second time. It lives on inside the boulevard, as the second half of one spread.
A right-hand paragraph floating in its own white space. Critic A named it twice; it is now the lead into the register.
Nine faces averaged as the first thing anyone saw. The idea was right and the picture was mud. Now it is earned by holding the shutter.
'On raw solargraph paper the sun burns dark.' Plate iv already says it in pictures.
'A star trail is mostly stars nobody named.' The caption under the trail already says it.
The newest instrument set at 5.61rem italic, louder than the sky it sits in. Down to the display size.
The oldest secret, retired to bring the store back to twenty.
A crystallization gene still listed in the genome, with no body to act on since gen 256.
